This might require new code for the single-node setup and integration with the existing module launcher.

U8 is about self-registering modules in service discovery. The user wants s-c-s modules to register themselves so that Spring XD can discover and orchestrate them. This involves integrating with service discovery tools (like Eureka or Consul) and modifying the modules to register themselves. The effort here would include adding service discovery clients to the modules and updating the orchestration logic in Spring XD.

For U1, fixing the NPE and integrating the Hortonworks Connector. Maybe 20 hours for debugging and 15 for integration. Total 35.

U3: Moving message-bus to spring-bus. This involves code extraction, updating dependencies, testing. Maybe 25 hours.

U4: Moving input/output type conversion. Similar to U3, maybe 20 hours.

U5: Moving serialization codec. Another 20 hours.

U6: Single-node implementation. This is a new feature. Maybe 30 hours for development and testing.

U7: Diego Receptor. This is more complex, involving CF integration. Maybe 40 hours.

U8: Self-registering modules. Adding service discovery. Maybe 25 hours.

Adding these up: 35 +10 +25 +20 +20 +30 +40 +25 = 205 hours. But I need to check if there are any overlaps or dependencies. For example, moving modules (U3, U4, U5) might have some shared tasks. But since they are separate components, probably separate efforts. Also, the single-node and Diego implementations (U6, U7) are separate. 

Technical decisions: For U1, using the Hortonworks Connector as a dependency. For U2, making the log directory a configurable property. For U3-U5, using Maven for dependency management. For U6, using the existing Module Launcher. For U7, integrating with Diego's APIs. For U8, using Spring Cloud for service discovery.

Assumptions: The Hortonworks Connector is compatible. The existing tests can be adapted. The service discovery is already set up in the environment. The code for moving modules is modular enough to extract.

For U6, implement a single-node admin SPI using the existing ModuleLauncher, bypassing distributed coordination for local execution.
For U7, develop a Diego-based Receptor implementation that interacts with Cloud Foundry's Diego runtime APIs to deploy modules.
For U8, integrate service discovery (e.g., Spring Cloud Netflix Eureka) into s-c-s modules to enable self-registration and dynamic orchestration.
assumptions: The Hortonworks Connector for Teradata is compatible with the current Sqoop version and requires minimal configuration.
The logging directory configuration change will not break existing logging behavior in non-RPM environments.
The modules being moved (message-bus, type conversion, serialization codec) are sufficiently decoupled to allow extraction without major refactoring.
The single-node implementation will reuse existing Spring XD infrastructure (e.g., ModuleLauncher) with minimal modifications.
Diego Receptor implementation will leverage existing CF Lattice/Diego APIs and require no additional infrastructure setup.
Service discovery integration will use Spring Cloud's existing service registry support (e.g., Eureka) and require no custom discovery logic.
